name: Rituximab
route_note: IV infusion; subcutaneous co-formulation with hyaluronidase for some lymphoma/CLL uses after a first IV dose

discovery.note: Chimeric mouse–human IgG1 derived from the murine anti-CD20 antibody 2B8.

tagline: The first monoclonal antibody approved for cancer; depletes CD20-positive B cells
summary: Rituximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody against CD20, a surface protein on most B cells. Approved in 1997 for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, it became a backbone of lymphoma and CLL therapy and is also used in rheumatoid arthritis, ANCA-associated vasculitis and pemphigus vulgaris.
mechanism: Rituximab binds CD20 (MS4A1), a membrane protein expressed from the pre-B to the mature B-cell stage but not on stem cells or plasma cells.

Bound antibody kills B cells through complement-dependent cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis by macrophages, and to some extent direct apoptosis. Because plasma cells lack CD20, existing antibody levels are only partly reduced, and B cells repopulate from precursors over 6–12 months.
uses: CD20-positive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (follicular, diffuse large B-cell)
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis

history.title: Antibody engineered
history.detail: IDEC creates the chimeric antibody IDEC-C2B8 from a murine anti-CD20 antibody.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Rituxan for relapsed or refractory low-grade or follicular B-cell NHL — the first monoclonal antibody approved for cancer.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU as MabThera, marketed by Roche.

history.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
history.detail: Approved for rheumatoid arthritis in combination with methotrexate.

history.title: CLL
history.detail: Approved for CLL with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide (FCR).

history.title: Vasculitis
history.detail: Approved for granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: Subcutaneous MabThera with hyaluronidase approved in the EU; Rituxan Hycela follows in the US in 2017.

history.title: First biosimilar
history.detail: The EU approves Truxima, the first rituximab biosimilar; the FDA approves it in 2018.

history.title: Pemphigus vulgaris
history.detail: FDA approves rituximab for moderate to severe pemphigus vulgaris.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

safety.boxed_warning: Fatal infusion-related reactions, severe mucocutaneous reactions, hepatitis B virus reactivation and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

facts: Rituximab was the first monoclonal antibody approved by the FDA to treat cancer.
B-cell depletion typically persists for 6–12 months after a course.
Patients should be screened for hepatitis B before treatment because of reactivation risk.
